title: Shooting review goes to Crown
article: An investigation into the police shooting of a Kamloops man has been forwarded to Crown counsel in Victoria for review.

A reviewing officer with the Kelowna RCMP serious crime unit has completed his probe into the June 27 shooting of Stephen Mace Hanaghan, 45, by a member of the Kamloops RCMP dog team, Kamloops RCMP Supt. Jim Begley said Thursday.
"This is a fairly routine thing. There was a lot of lab evidence with this case. It's good to get a third-eye independent review," he said.
Begley expects it will be two to three months before it is known if any charges will be laid against the officer.
Hanaghan was shot and killed moments after he backed a 1984 red and white Chevy into an RCMP Suburban on Noble Lake Road.
He and a 45-year-old male passenger were pursued through Westsyde by police after witnesses spotted them breaking into a Super Save gas station on Westsyde Road.
